edges.description: Shown in Tsga10 heterozygous mice. In patients the two findings are reported together but not causally linked.
Headless tails cannot fertilize an oocyte, so natural conception is not possible.
The mice reproduce the disordered mitochondrial sheath seen in patient sperm.
edges.limitations: The mouse defect appears with one null allele, while human disease is recessive, and the abstract does not report headless sperm, so the model does not show the defining acephalic phenotype.

nodes.description: The defining finding. The ejaculate contains mostly headless sperm tails, up to 99% of spermatozoa, with a few loose heads.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report a 27 years old infertile male from a consanguineous family, who presented with 99% headless sperm in his ejaculate.

nodes.description: TSGA10 is a centrosomal scaffold protein whose C-terminal fragment sits at the centrosome and basal body and binds ODF2, so it is thought to help anchor the sperm tail to the head. Without it, the flagellum separates from the head at a point between the distal centriole and the midpiece.

nodes.description: ICSI with the few remaining heads is the only route to biological paternity. Outcomes in TSGA10 cases differ between reports: the first patient's embryos were of poor quality and no pregnancy followed, while a later Chinese cohort with TSGA10 or PMFBP1 variants reported good ICSI outcomes.

evidence.reference_title: Patients with acephalic spermatozoa syndrome linked to novel TSGA10/PMFBP1 variants have favorable pregnancy outcomes from intracytoplasmic sperm injection.
evidence.snippet: Patients with TSGA10/PMFBP1 variations were all expected to have good prognoses with ICSI.

evidence.snippet: One cycle of in vitro fertilization-assisted reproduction was conducted, but pregnancy was not achieved after embryo transfer, possibly due to poor embryo quality.

nodes.description: Frameshift, splice-site and missense variants all leave spermatozoa without detectable TSGA10. The frameshift alleles truncate the protein, the splice variant produces a truncated protein at very low level, and the Leu371Pro missense variant abolishes both mRNA and protein in sperm. TSGA10 is normally found at the sperm midpiece. In mouse testis the 65-kDa spermatid protein is processed to a 27-kDa fibrous sheath protein.

evidence.reference_title: TSGA10 is a novel candidate gene associated with acephalic spermatozoa.
evidence.snippet: TSGA10 is a testis-specific protein that localized to the midpiece in the spermatozoa of a normal control; however, immunostaining failed to detect TSGA10 protein in the patient's sperm. Western blot analysis also showed complete absence of TSGA10 protein in the patient.
